title: Tight Regular-Indifferentiability Bound for Permutation Sums
summary: For two public n-bit permutations, the proven bound is two to the two-n-thirds divided by n; closing the gap to the two-to-five-n-sixths-query attack threshold remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine the tight regular-indifferentiability security bound for the sum of two independent public $n$-bit permutations, including whether the gap between the proven bound $2^{2n/3}/n$ and the generic uniform-simulator attack threshold of $2^{5n/6}$ queries can be closed.

scope.domain: Regular indifferentiability and query security for sums of public permutations in symmetric cryptography.
assumptions: The two public n-bit permutations are independent.
parameters: n: bit length of each permutation and exponent scale in the security bounds
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the tight security bound and whether the gap between the proven bound and the generic uniform-simulator attack threshold can be closed.

citations.label: Revisiting the Indifferentiability of the Sum of Permutations

progress.summary: The paper explicitly leaves the tightness of indifferentiability for the sum of permutations open. It contrasts a proven bound of 2^(2n/3)/n with a generic uniform-simulator attack threshold of 2^(5n/6) queries.
citation_labels: Aldo Gunsing et al., Revisiting the Indifferentiability of the Sum of Permutations
